addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Use when the user asks to create AgentSight insights, artifact reports, shareable investigation pages, monitor summaries, usage summaries, failure/resource findings, or Claude Code artifact-like reports for AgentSight traces.

Use when checking cross-section alignment, naming drift, contradictions with artifacts, or unsupported claims introduced in a passage; complements critique and targeted-fix skills.
- auto-research-orchestrator: Orchestrate or resume a research project from idea to paper submission. Use when the user asks what research stage they are in, what gate blocks progress, how to resume after context loss, what the next research action is, or which specialist workflow should run next. Applies across systems, ML, agents, measurement, infrastructure, and empirical research. Do not use for standalone prose editing, a single experiment-design request, a one-off literature summary, or ordinary paper review unless the user asks for lifecycle routing or gate decisions.
- check-paper-citations: Verify every citation in a paper is real, accurate, and correctly used. Downloads PDFs, reads abstracts, checks claims against source text, flags AI-hallucinated references, identifies uncited claims, and maintains structured annotations in the .bib file. Use when the user says "check citations", "verify references", "are these citations real", or when iter-refine-writing finds unannotated bib entries. Also use before submission as a final citation gate.
- check-paper-structure-flow: Check a systems paper's structure at macro level (sections, subsections) and micro level (paragraph roles, sentence flow). Covers section organization, intro/abstract paragraph conventions, design/impl separation, and within-section flow for 12-page full papers, 6-page workshop papers, and 2-page extended abstracts. Use when the user asks to check paper structure, section organization, paragraph flow, or whether the paper follows OSDI/SOSP conventions. Also use as Rounds 0-2 of iter-refine-writing.
- check-terminology-infoflow: Audit terminology, invented jargon, concept consistency, and information flow across a LaTeX paper. Catches the deep readability problems that sentence-level style checks miss.
- critique-like-senior-systems-reviewer: Critiques a selected LaTeX section as a skeptical senior SOSP/OSDI reviewer, separating writing vs logic vs technical vs evidence gaps, ranking severity, and giving concrete fixes. Use when the user asks for a systems-style critique, reviewer simulation, section review, or "OSDI/SOSP reviewer" feedback on introduction, design, evaluation, related work, or any subsection.
- iter-refine-writing: Iteratively refine the WRITING of a systems paper through 11 serial review-fix rounds. Covers macro structure, micro structure, section conventions, logic flow, abstract/intro rebuild, consistency, language (3 passes), terminology/claim tone, and citation verification. Does not handle claims, research framing, or scope — those belong to the orchestrator or dedicated skills. Use when the user says "iterate on the writing", "polish the paper", "fix the prose", "run a few rounds of review", or "improve the writing". Works with LaTeX papers targeting any systems venue. Part of the auto-research pipeline; run after iter-refine-writing-idea.
- iter-refine-writing-idea: Iteratively refine the IDEA LAYER of a systems paper — contribution statements, insight framing, novelty claims, problem framing, and design goal alignment. Does not handle experiments, prose quality, or section structure — those belong to other skills. Use when the user says "refine the contributions", "is the framing right", "check the insight", "are the claims well-stated", or wants to iterate on how the paper's ideas are expressed. Five mandatory serial rounds of subagent review — no skipping. Part of the auto-research pipeline; run before iter-refine-writing.

Do not use for ordinary feature/bug implementation, issue triage, or paper prose review.

Do not use for ordinary feature changes in an existing repo, release preparation, or CI debugging.
- rebuttal: Draft and audit grounded academic rebuttals after external reviews arrive. Use when the user provides reviewer comments, meta-review text, OpenReview/CMT/HotCRP author-response constraints, an existing rebuttal draft, or asks for rebuttal strategy, concern coverage, per-reviewer responses, follow-up replies, or a revision promise checklist. Works for systems, ML, agents, measurement, and empirical research papers. Do not use for ordinary pre-submission paper review without external reviews.

Use when planning a paper evaluation, mapping claims to experiments, choosing baselines/metrics/workloads/datasets, designing ablations, scalability, fault-injection, robustness, statistical validity checks, benchmark methodology, experiment run order, or checking whether results are strong enough for venues such as OSDI/SOSP/NSDI/EuroSys/ICML/NeurIPS/ICLR/SIGMETRICS.

Applies across systems, ML, agents, measurement, infrastructure, and empirical research.

- agent-interaction-insights: Analyze agent transcripts and traces to recommend collaboration improvements and generate decision-oriented HTML reports. - Use when the user asks to analyze agent sessions, reduce corrections, improve trust, stop retry loops, compare agents, or generate insights from Claude/Codex/Gemini logs, OTel spans, or LangSmith/Langfuse exports.

Use when the user asks for an artifact, investigation report, team brief, reviewer note, or Claude Code Insights-style page about AI agent behavior.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

560	\subsection{RQ1: Does Semantic Profiling Improve Resource Attribution?}
561	% RQ1：语义分析能否改善资源归因？
562	
563	The strongest argument against semantic profiling is that traditional tools ``can already see the same information.''
564	% 反对语义分析的最强论点是传统工具"已经能看到相同信息"。
565	To test this, we run a semantic-axis ablation on 325 real Codex/Claude trajectories (183{,}714 system observations).
566	% 为了检验这一点，我们在 325 个真实 Codex/Claude 会话（183,714 个系统观测）上进行语义轴消融。
567	We progressively add tag axes (no tags, session only, prompt only, both) and measure the mixed-weight percentage, the fraction of system-effect cost in groups that mix observations from multiple task categories.
568	% 我们逐步添加标签轴（无标签、仅会话、仅提示词、两者兼有），测量混合权重百分比——混合了多个任务类别观测的桶中的系统副作用权重比例。
569	A lower mixed-weight percentage means the profiler correctly separates effects by task category.
570	% 更低的混合权重百分比意味着分析器正确地按任务类别分离了效果。
571	The residual percentage measures weight in groups where the majority category accounts for less than 90\% of the group, capturing partial mixing.
572	% 残余百分比测量多数类别占桶内不到 90\% 的权重，捕获部分混合。
573	
574	\begin{table}[t]
575	\centering\small
576	\caption{Semantic-axis ablation on 183{,}714 system observations
577	from 325 real trajectories. All rows preserve the same total weight.}
578	\label{tab:mixing}
579	\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
580	\toprule
581	Projection & Unique stacks & Mixed weight \% & Residual \% \\
582	\midrule
583	No semantic tags & 11{,}967 & 90.4 & 44.7 \\
584	Session tag only & 15{,}027 & 84.4 & 33.4 \\
585	Prompt tag only & 24{,}703 & 36.7 & 7.5 \\
586	Session + prompt & 26{,}829 & 0.0 & 0.0 \\
587	\bottomrule
588	\end{tabular}
589	\end{table}
590	
591	Table~\ref{tab:mixing} shows the result on 325 real Codex/Claude trajectories.
592	% Table~\ref{tab:mixing} 展示了 325 个真实 Codex/Claude 会话上的结果。
593	Without semantic tags, 90.4\% of system-effect cost falls into mixed groups.
594	% 没有语义标签时，90.4\% 的系统副作用权重落入混合桶。
595	A flat \texttt{cargo~test} counter shows 2{,}903 executions but cannot distinguish whether they came from \texttt{review}, \texttt{debug}, \texttt{refactor}, or \texttt{test} prompts.
596	% 扁平的 \texttt{cargo test} 计数器显示 2,903 次执行，但无法区分它们来自 \texttt{review}、\texttt{debug}、\texttt{refactor} 还是 \texttt{test} 提示词。
597	Adding only the prompt tag reduces mixed weight to 36.7\% and residual to 7.5\%.
598	% 仅添加提示词标签就将混合权重降至 36.7\%，残余降至 7.5\%。
599	The session tag alone barely helps (84.4\%), because trajectories typically contain multiple intent phases.
600	% 仅会话标签几乎没有帮助（84.4\%），因为会话通常包含多个意图阶段。
601	
602	A tag-permutation test (1{,}000 shuffles, $p = 0.001$) confirms the separation is not random.
603	% 标签置换测试（1,000 次洗牌，$p = 0.001$）确认分离不是随机的。
604	Semantic-tag quality is validated in RQ3.
605	% 语义标签质量在 RQ3 中验证。
606	
607	Beyond tag separation, we test whether choosing different field selections for the operation stack produces views that flat grouping cannot.
608	% 除标签分离外，我们还测试为 operation stack 选择不同字段是否产生扁平分组无法产生的视图。
609	We take the same 13{,}265 operations from the four oracle-rich families and fold them with five different field selections, counting how many distinct groups each produces.
610	% 我们取四个 oracle 丰富家族的同样 13,265 个 operation，用五种不同字段选择折叠，计算每种产生多少不同分组。
611	The same operations fold into 9~dataset groups, 57~phase groups, 226~semantic groups, 455~action groups, or 3{,}757~per-session groups by changing only the stack fields.
612	% 同样的 operation 仅通过改变栈字段即可折叠为 9 个数据集分组、57 个阶段分组、226 个语义分组、455 个操作分组或 3,757 个固定会话分组。
613	A flat GROUP BY on a single tag cannot produce these views because different stack depths answer different questions (budget by task vs.\ duplication by action vs.\ per-session detail).

\subsection{RQ1: Does Semantic Profiling Improve Resource Attribution?}
% RQ1：语义分析能否改善资源归因？

The strongest argument against semantic profiling is that traditional tools ``can already see the same information.''
% 反对语义分析的最强论点是传统工具"已经能看到相同信息"。
To test this, we run a semantic-axis ablation on 325 real Codex/Claude trajectories (183{,}714 system observations).
% 为了检验这一点，我们在 325 个真实 Codex/Claude 会话（183,714 个系统观测）上进行语义轴消融。
We progressively add tag axes (no tags, session only, prompt only, both) and measure the mixed-weight percentage, the fraction of system-effect cost in groups that mix observations from multiple task categories.
% 我们逐步添加标签轴（无标签、仅会话、仅提示词、两者兼有），测量混合权重百分比——混合了多个任务类别观测的桶中的系统副作用权重比例。
A lower mixed-weight percentage means the profiler correctly separates effects by task category.
% 更低的混合权重百分比意味着分析器正确地按任务类别分离了效果。
The residual percentage measures weight in groups where the majority category accounts for less than 90\% of the group, capturing partial mixing.
% 残余百分比测量多数类别占桶内不到 90\% 的权重，捕获部分混合。

\begin{table}[t]
\centering\small
\caption{Semantic-axis ablation on 183{,}714 system observations
from 325 real trajectories. All rows preserve the same total weight.}
\label{tab:mixing}
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
Projection & Unique stacks & Mixed weight \% & Residual \% \\
\midrule
No semantic tags & 11{,}967 & 90.4 & 44.7 \\
Session tag only & 15{,}027 & 84.4 & 33.4 \\
Prompt tag only & 24{,}703 & 36.7 & 7.5 \\
Session + prompt & 26{,}829 & 0.0 & 0.0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Table~\ref{tab:mixing} shows the result on 325 real Codex/Claude trajectories.
% Table~\ref{tab:mixing} 展示了 325 个真实 Codex/Claude 会话上的结果。
Without semantic tags, 90.4\% of system-effect cost falls into mixed groups.
% 没有语义标签时，90.4\% 的系统副作用权重落入混合桶。
A flat \texttt{cargo~test} counter shows 2{,}903 executions but cannot distinguish whether they came from \texttt{review}, \texttt{debug}, \texttt{refactor}, or \texttt{test} prompts.
% 扁平的 \texttt{cargo test} 计数器显示 2,903 次执行，但无法区分它们来自 \texttt{review}、\texttt{debug}、\texttt{refactor} 还是 \texttt{test} 提示词。
Adding only the prompt tag reduces mixed weight to 36.7\% and residual to 7.5\%.
% 仅添加提示词标签就将混合权重降至 36.7\%，残余降至 7.5\%。
The session tag alone barely helps (84.4\%), because trajectories typically contain multiple intent phases.
% 仅会话标签几乎没有帮助（84.4\%），因为会话通常包含多个意图阶段。

A tag-permutation test (1{,}000 shuffles, $p = 0.001$) confirms the separation is not random.
% 标签置换测试（1,000 次洗牌，$p = 0.001$）确认分离不是随机的。
Semantic-tag quality is validated in RQ3.
% 语义标签质量在 RQ3 中验证。

Beyond tag separation, we test whether choosing different field selections for the operation stack produces views that flat grouping cannot.
% 除标签分离外，我们还测试为 operation stack 选择不同字段是否产生扁平分组无法产生的视图。
We take the same 13{,}265 operations from the four oracle-rich families and fold them with five different field selections, counting how many distinct groups each produces.
% 我们取四个 oracle 丰富家族的同样 13,265 个 operation，用五种不同字段选择折叠，计算每种产生多少不同分组。
The same operations fold into 9~dataset groups, 57~phase groups, 226~semantic groups, 455~action groups, or 3{,}757~per-session groups by changing only the stack fields.
% 同样的 operation 仅通过改变栈字段即可折叠为 9 个数据集分组、57 个阶段分组、226 个语义分组、455 个操作分组或 3,757 个固定会话分组。
A flat GROUP BY on a single tag cannot produce these views because different stack depths answer different questions (budget by task vs.\ duplication by action vs.\ per-session detail).
% 单标签的扁平 GROUP BY 无法产生这些视图，因为不同栈深度回答不同问题（任务级预算 vs. 操作级重复 vs. 会话级下钻）。
The same model also covers all 15 public trace families (Table~\ref{tab:datasets}) without type-specific objects.
% 同一模型也覆盖了所有 15 个公开 trace 家族（Table~\ref{tab:datasets}），无需特定类型对象。

Different views also produce different rankings.
% 不同视图也产生不同排名。

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate RQ1 and RQ3 figures for the AgentPProf paper."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 10,
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'figure.figsize': (3.5, 2.5),
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.alpha': 0.3,
})

BLUE = '#2196F3'
RED = '#E57373'
GRAY = '#9E9E9E'


def make_rq1_separation():
    labels = ['No labels', 'Session\nonly', 'Prompt\nonly', 'Session\n+ Prompt']
    mixed = [90.4, 84.4, 36.7, 0.0]
    separated = [9.6, 15.6, 63.3, 100.0]

    x = np.arange(len(labels))
    width = 0.55

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.2))
    ax.bar(x, mixed, width, label='Mixed', color=RED, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')
    ax.bar(x, separated, width, bottom=mixed, label='Separated', color=BLUE, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax.set_ylabel('Weight (%)')
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 105)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)

    for i, (m, s) in enumerate(zip(mixed, separated)):
        if m > 10:
            ax.text(i, m / 2, f'{m:.1f}%', ha='center', va='center', fontsize=7, color='white', fontweight='bold')

    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq1-separation.pdf/png')


def make_rq3_vmeasure():
    datasets = ['mind2web', 'webshop', 'swe-agent', 'weblinx',
                'agenttrek', 'gui-odyssey', 'android', 'toolbench', 'api-bank']
    vmeasure = [1.000, 1.000, 0.926, 0.872, 0.862, 0.811, 0.716, 0.134, 0.000]

    colors = [BLUE if v >= 0.7 else GRAY for v in vmeasure]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.2))
    x = np.arange(len(datasets))
    bars = ax.bar(x, vmeasure, 0.6, color=colors, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax.axhline(y=0.7, color=RED, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2, label='Threshold (0.7)')
    ax.set_ylabel('V-measure')
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(datasets, fontsize=6.5, rotation=35, ha='right')
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.12)
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate RQ1 and RQ3 figures for the AgentPProf paper."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 10,
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'figure.figsize': (3.5, 2.5),
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.alpha': 0.3,
})

BLUE = '#2196F3'
RED = '#E57373'
GRAY = '#9E9E9E'


def make_rq1_separation():
    labels = ['No labels', 'Session\nonly', 'Prompt\nonly', 'Session\n+ Prompt']
    mixed = [90.4, 84.4, 36.7, 0.0]
    separated = [9.6, 15.6, 63.3, 100.0]

    x = np.arange(len(labels))
    width = 0.55

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.2))
    ax.bar(x, mixed, width, label='Mixed', color=RED, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')
    ax.bar(x, separated, width, bottom=mixed, label='Separated', color=BLUE, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax.set_ylabel('Weight (%)')
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 105)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)

    for i, (m, s) in enumerate(zip(mixed, separated)):
        if m > 10:
            ax.text(i, m / 2, f'{m:.1f}%', ha='center', va='center', fontsize=7, color='white', fontweight='bold')

    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq1-separation.pdf/png')


def make_rq3_vmeasure():
    datasets = ['mind2web', 'webshop', 'swe-agent', 'weblinx',
                'agenttrek', 'gui-odyssey', 'android', 'toolbench', 'api-bank']
    vmeasure = [1.000, 1.000, 0.926, 0.872, 0.862, 0.811, 0.716, 0.134, 0.000]

    colors = [BLUE if v >= 0.7 else GRAY for v in vmeasure]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.2))
    x = np.arange(len(datasets))
    bars = ax.bar(x, vmeasure, 0.6, color=colors, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax.axhline(y=0.7, color=RED, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2, label='Threshold (0.7)')
    ax.set_ylabel('V-measure')
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(datasets, fontsize=6.5, rotation=35, ha='right')
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.12)
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)

    for i, v in enumerate(vmeasure):
        if v > 0.05:
            ax.text(i, v + 0.02, f'{v:.2f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=6)

    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('fig-rq3-vmeasure.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq3-vmeasure.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq3-vmeasure.pdf/png')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    make_rq1_separation()
    make_rq3_vmeasure()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate RQ1 and RQ3 figures for the AgentPProf paper."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 10,
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'figure.figsize': (3.5, 2.5),
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.alpha': 0.3,
})

BLUE = '#2196F3'
RED = '#E57373'
GRAY = '#9E9E9E'


def make_rq1_separation():
    labels = ['No semantic\ntags', 'Session\ntag only', 'Prompt\ntag only', 'Session\n+ Prompt']
    mixed = [90.4, 84.4, 36.7, 0.0]
    residual = [44.7, 33.4, 7.5, 0.0]
    stacks = [11967, 15027, 24703, 26829]

    x = np.arange(len(labels))
    width = 0.28

    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.5))

    b1 = ax1.bar(x - width/2, mixed, width, label='Mixed weight %',
                 color=RED, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')
    b2 = ax1.bar(x + width/2, residual, width, label='Residual %',
                 color='#FFAB91', alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax1.set_ylabel('Percentage (%)', fontsize=8)
    ax1.set_xticks(x)
    ax1.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=7)
    ax1.set_ylim(0, 108)
    ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

    for i, m in enumerate(mixed):
        if m > 5:
            ax1.text(i - width/2, m + 1.5, f'{m:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                     fontsize=6, color=RED, fontweight='bold')
    for i, r in enumerate(residual):
        if r > 5:
            ax1.text(i + width/2, r + 1.5, f'{r:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                     fontsize=6, color='#E64A19', fontweight='bold')

    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    ax2.plot(x, [s/1000 for s in stacks], 'o-', color=BLUE, linewidth=1.5,
             markersize=4, label='Unique stacks (k)', zorder=5)
    ax2.set_ylabel('Unique stacks (thousands)', fontsize=8)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 32)
    ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

    for i, s in enumerate(stacks):
        ax2.text(i, s/1000 + 0.8, f'{s/1000:.1f}k', ha='center', va='bottom',
                 fontsize=6, color=BLUE, fontweight='bold')

    h1, l1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
    h2, l2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
    ax1.legend(h1 + h2, l1 + l2, fontsize=6.5, loc='upper center',
               ncol=3, framealpha=0.9, columnspacing=0.8)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq1-separation.pdf/png')


def make_rq3_vmeasure():
    datasets = ['mind2web', 'webshop', 'swe-agent', 'weblinx',
                'agenttrek', 'gui-odyssey', 'android', 'toolbench', 'api-bank']
    vmeasure = [1.000, 1.000, 0.926, 0.872, 0.862, 0.811, 0.716, 0.134, 0.000]

    colors = [BLUE if v >= 0.7 else GRAY for v in vmeasure]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.2))
    x = np.arange(len(datasets))
    bars = ax.bar(x, vmeasure, 0.6, color=colors, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax.axhline(y=0.7, color=RED, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2, label='Threshold (0.7)')
    ax.set_ylabel('V-measure')
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(datasets, fontsize=6.5, rotation=35, ha='right')
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.12)
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)

    for i, v in enumerate(vmeasure):
        if v > 0.05:
            ax.text(i, v + 0.02, f'{v:.2f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=6)

    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('fig-rq3-vmeasure.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq3-vmeasure.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq3-vmeasure.pdf/png')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    make_rq1_separation()
    make_rq3_vmeasure()

599	The session tag alone barely helps (84.4\%), because trajectories typically contain multiple intent phases.

603	% 标签置换测试（1,000 次洗牌，$p = 0.001$）确认分离不是随机的。

611	The same operations fold into 9~dataset groups, 57~phase groups, 226~semantic groups, 455~action groups, or 3{,}757~per-session groups by changing only the stack fields.
612	% 同样的 operation 仅通过改变栈字段即可折叠为 9 个数据集分组、57 个阶段分组、226 个语义分组、455 个操作分组或 3,757 个固定会话分组。
613	A flat GROUP BY on a single tag cannot produce these views because different stack depths answer different questions (budget by task vs.\ duplication by action vs.\ per-session detail).
614	% 单标签的扁平 GROUP BY 无法产生这些视图，因为不同栈深度回答不同问题（任务级预算 vs. 操作级重复 vs. 会话级下钻）。
615	The same model also covers all 15 public trace families (Table~\ref{tab:datasets}) without type-specific objects.
616	% 同一模型也覆盖了所有 15 个公开 trace 家族（Table~\ref{tab:datasets}），无需特定类型对象。
617

619	% 不同视图也产生不同排名。

622	\texttt{network}-tagged prompts rank 8th by time (I/O wait) but 93rd by tokens, showing that the choice of weight function changes the analysis conclusions.
623	% \texttt{network} 标记的提示词按时间排第 8（I/O 等待）但按 token 排第 93，表明权重函数的选择改变了分析结论。

628	% 我们在 RQ2 使用的同样六个任务上运行自动栈诱导模式（\S\ref{sec:stacks}），将结果的分组数和定位质量与扁平摘要和固定会话下钻进行比较。
629	Induced stacks produce a median of 12 groups (versus 285 for per-session and 1 for flat), with 4/6 tasks generating variable-depth stacks.
630	% 诱导栈产生中位 12 个分组（固定会话 285 个，扁平 1 个），4/6 任务生成可变深度栈。
631	The induced stacks achieve lower AP than hand-configured stacks (median 0.276 vs 0.312) because they use only visible fields, but they reduce inspection work to 65.3\% versus flat summaries without requiring any user configuration.
632	% 诱导栈的 AP 低于手动配置栈（中位 0.276 vs 0.312），因为它们仅使用可见字段，但将检查工作量降至扁平摘要的 65.3\%，无需任何用户配置。

---
name: paper-figures
description: Create, audit, and improve figures in systems papers. Covers both design diagrams (architecture, flow, component) and result plots (bar charts, line plots, heatmaps). Checks figure-text alignment, abstraction level, claim support, and visual clarity. Use when the user says "draw an architecture diagram", "make a figure", "check the figures", "improve the plots", or when iter-refine-writing flags a missing diagram. Design diagrams use TikZ or draw.io; result plots are always drawn with Python (matplotlib).
---

# Paper Figures

Create and audit figures for systems papers. Two types of figures have different rules — read the corresponding reference before creating or reviewing.

## First Step

Determine the figure type:
- **Design diagram** (architecture, flow, component, trust boundary) → read `references/design-diagrams.md`
- **Result plot** (bar chart, line plot, CDF, heatmap, table-as-figure) → read `references/result-plots.md`

If auditing existing figures, read both references and check every figure in the paper.

## Audit Checklist (for all figures)

1. **Does every figure support a specific claim?** Identify which claim in the text the figure supports. If no claim, the figure may be unnecessary.
2. **Is the figure referenced in the text?** Every figure must have a `\ref{}` in the prose that explains what the reader should see.
3. **Is the caption self-contained?** A reader should understand the figure from caption alone without reading the body text.
4. **Do labels match the text?** Component names, axis labels, and legend entries must use the same terms as the prose.
5. **Is the abstraction level correct?** Design diagrams in the Design section should be mechanism-agnostic. Implementation details belong in Implementation section figures.
6. **Does every RQ / experiment block have at least one figure?** An RQ represented only by tables is a red flag. If the point is a comparison, trend, distribution, or scaling behavior, convert the table to a plot (bar/line/CDF/heatmap) and keep at most the key exact values in text or an appendix table. Tables stay tables only when exact values, feature matrices, or many discrete configuration dimensions are the point.

## LaTeX Placement Mechanics

Figure content and figure placement fail independently — check both. For two-column papers:

- **Wide figures span both columns**: use `figure*` (and `table*`); a wide figure squeezed into one column is unreadable. `figure*` cannot use `[h]`; it floats to the top of a page.
- **Side-by-side needs a width check**: two subfigures sharing one column are usually too small to read. If labels drop below ~7pt effective size, stack them or promote to `figure*`.
- **Default to `[t]`** placement; `[h]` fights LaTeX and loses.
- **Pinning a figure to a specific page** (e.g. architecture figure on page 2): place the float's source just after the first paragraph of the page-2 content, use `[t!]`, and let text (even a citation-heavy paragraph) flow to the next page instead — text can move, the figure anchor should not. Verify the final PDF page after every recompile that touches floats.
- **After any float change, recheck page budget and margins** — floats are the usual cause of text-height overflows.

## Result Plots Are Python-Drawn

Every numeric/result figure — RQ figures, bar charts, line plots, CDFs, heatmaps — is generated by a Python script (matplotlib) that reads the result data files. Never pgfplots, never hand-placed TikZ coordinates, never numbers typed into the figure by hand: if a value changes in the results, rerunning the script must regenerate the figure. Keep the script and its data paths in the repo next to the figures so any plot can be reproduced; LaTeX includes the generated PDF/PNG. TikZ and draw.io are for design diagrams only.

## Creating Figures

When creating a new figure:
1. Read the relevant reference file
2. Ask: what claim does this figure support?
3. Draft the figure (TikZ/draw.io for design diagrams; a Python matplotlib script for result plots, per the rule above)
4. Check against the reference's checklist
5. Write a self-contained caption
6. Add `\ref{}` in the text where the figure is discussed
7. Compile and verify page count

name: paper-figures
description: Create, audit, and improve figures in systems papers. Covers both design diagrams (architecture, flow, component) and result plots (bar charts, line plots, heatmaps). Checks figure-text alignment, abstraction level, claim support, and visual clarity. Use when the user says "draw an architecture diagram", "make a figure", "check the figures", "improve the plots", or when iter-refine-writing flags a missing diagram. Design diagrams use TikZ or draw.io; result plots are always drawn with Python (matplotlib).

# Paper Figures

Create and audit figures for systems papers. Two types of figures have different rules — read the corresponding reference before creating or reviewing.

## First Step

Determine the figure type:
- **Design diagram** (architecture, flow, component, trust boundary) → read `references/design-diagrams.md`
- **Result plot** (bar chart, line plot, CDF, heatmap, table-as-figure) → read `references/result-plots.md`

If auditing existing figures, read both references and check every figure in the paper.

## Audit Checklist (for all figures)

1. **Does every figure support a specific claim?** Identify which claim in the text the figure supports. If no claim, the figure may be unnecessary.
2. **Is the figure referenced in the text?** Every figure must have a `\ref{}` in the prose that explains what the reader should see.
3. **Is the caption self-contained?** A reader should understand the figure from caption alone without reading the body text.
4. **Do labels match the text?** Component names, axis labels, and legend entries must use the same terms as the prose.
5. **Is the abstraction level correct?** Design diagrams in the Design section should be mechanism-agnostic. Implementation details belong in Implementation section figures.
6. **Does every RQ / experiment block have at least one figure?** An RQ represented only by tables is a red flag. If the point is a comparison, trend, distribution, or scaling behavior, convert the table to a plot (bar/line/CDF/heatmap) and keep at most the key exact values in text or an appendix table. Tables stay tables only when exact values, feature matrices, or many discrete configuration dimensions are the point.
7. **No redundant table + figure for the same small dataset.** When a figure already shows all values from a table (especially tables with fewer than ~6 rows), delete the table and fold all data into the figure — annotate bars/lines with exact values if needed. Duplicate presentation wastes page budget and forces the reader to cross-reference two floats for the same point. Keep the table only if it has many columns or exact values that the figure cannot legibly show.

## LaTeX Placement Mechanics

Figure content and figure placement fail independently — check both. For two-column papers:

- **Wide figures span both columns**: use `figure*` (and `table*`); a wide figure squeezed into one column is unreadable. `figure*` cannot use `[h]`; it floats to the top of a page.
- **Side-by-side needs a width check**: two subfigures sharing one column are usually too small to read. If labels drop below ~7pt effective size, stack them or promote to `figure*`.
- **Default to `[t]`** placement; `[h]` fights LaTeX and loses.
- **Pinning a figure to a specific page** (e.g. architecture figure on page 2): place the float's source just after the first paragraph of the page-2 content, use `[t!]`, and let text (even a citation-heavy paragraph) flow to the next page instead — text can move, the figure anchor should not. Verify the final PDF page after every recompile that touches floats.
- **After any float change, recheck page budget and margins** — floats are the usual cause of text-height overflows.

## Result Plots Are Python-Drawn

Every numeric/result figure — RQ figures, bar charts, line plots, CDFs, heatmaps — is generated by a Python script (matplotlib) that reads the result data files. Never pgfplots, never hand-placed TikZ coordinates, never numbers typed into the figure by hand: if a value changes in the results, rerunning the script must regenerate the figure. Keep the script and its data paths in the repo next to the figures so any plot can be reproduced; LaTeX includes the generated PDF/PNG. TikZ and draw.io are for design diagrams only.

## Creating Figures

When creating a new figure:
1. Read the relevant reference file
2. Ask: what claim does this figure support?
3. Draft the figure (TikZ/draw.io for design diagrams; a Python matplotlib script for result plots, per the rule above)
4. Check against the reference's checklist
5. Write a self-contained caption
6. Add `\ref{}` in the text where the figure is discussed
7. Compile and verify page count

1	---
2	name: paper-figures
3	description: Create, audit, and improve figures in systems papers. Covers both design diagrams (architecture, flow, component) and result plots (bar charts, line plots, heatmaps). Checks figure-text alignment, abstraction level, claim support, and visual clarity. Use when the user says "draw an architecture diagram", "make a figure", "check the figures", "improve the plots", or when iter-refine-writing flags a missing diagram. Design diagrams use TikZ or draw.io; result plots are always drawn with Python (matplotlib).
4	---
5	
6	# Paper Figures
7	
8	Create and audit figures for systems papers. Two types of figures have different rules — read the corresponding reference before creating or reviewing.
9	
10	## First Step
11	
12	Determine the figure type:
13	- **Design diagram** (architecture, flow, component, trust boundary) → read `references/design-diagrams.md`
14	- **Result plot** (bar chart, line plot, CDF, heatmap, table-as-figure) → read `references/result-plots.md`
15	
16	If auditing existing figures, read both references and check every figure in the paper.
17	
18	## Audit Checklist (for all figures)
19	
20	1. **Does every figure support a specific claim?** Identify which claim in the text the figure supports. If no claim, the figure may be unnecessary.
21	2. **Is the figure referenced in the text?** Every figure must have a `\ref{}` in the prose that explains what the reader should see.
22	3. **Is the caption self-contained?** A reader should understand the figure from caption alone without reading the body text.
23	4. **Do labels match the text?** Component names, axis labels, and legend entries must use the same terms as the prose.
24	5. **Is the abstraction level correct?** Design diagrams in the Design section should be mechanism-agnostic. Implementation details belong in Implementation section figures.
25	6. **Does every RQ / experiment block have at least one figure?** An RQ represented only by tables is a red flag. If the point is a comparison, trend, distribution, or scaling behavior, convert the table to a plot (bar/line/CDF/heatmap) and keep at most the key exact values in text or an appendix table. Tables stay tables only when exact values, feature matrices, or many discrete configuration dimensions are the point.
26	7. **Same RQ, same data → one float only.** Within a single RQ or experiment block, the same dataset must not appear as both a table and a figure. Pick the format that best serves the claim: a figure for trends, comparisons, and distributions; a table for exact values, feature matrices, or many discrete dimensions. If a figure needs exact numbers, annotate its bars/lines instead of adding a companion table. Duplicate presentation wastes page budget and forces the reader to cross-reference two floats for the same point.
27	
28	## LaTeX Placement Mechanics
29	
30	Figure content and figure placement fail independently — check both. For two-column papers:
31	
32	- **Wide figures span both columns**: use `figure*` (and `table*`); a wide figure squeezed into one column is unreadable. `figure*` cannot use `[h]`; it floats to the top of a page.
33	- **Side-by-side needs a width check**: two subfigures sharing one column are usually too small to read. If labels drop below ~7pt effective size, stack them or promote to `figure*`.
34	- **Default to `[t]`** placement; `[h]` fights LaTeX and loses.
35	- **Pinning a figure to a specific page** (e.g. architecture figure on page 2): place the float's source just after the first paragraph of the page-2 content, use `[t!]`, and let text (even a citation-heavy paragraph) flow to the next page instead — text can move, the figure anchor should not. Verify the final PDF page after every recompile that touches floats.
36	- **After any float change, recheck page budget and margins** — floats are the usual cause of text-height overflows.
37	
38	## Result Plots Are Python-Drawn
39	
40	Every numeric/result figure — RQ figures, bar charts, line plots, CDFs, heatmaps — is generated by a Python script (matplotlib) that reads the result data files. Never pgfplots, never hand-placed TikZ coordinates, never numbers typed into the figure by hand: if a value changes in the results, rerunning the script must regenerate the figure. Create and audit figures for systems papers. Two types of figures have different rules — read the corresponding reference before creating or reviewing.

1. **Does every figure support a specific claim?** Identify which claim in the text the figure supports. If no claim, the figure may be unnecessary.
2. **Is the figure referenced in the text?** Every figure must have a `\ref{}` in the prose that explains what the reader should see.

5. **Is the abstraction level correct?** Design diagrams in the Design section should be mechanism-agnostic. Implementation details belong in Implementation section figures.
6. **Does every RQ / experiment block have at least one figure?** An RQ represented only by tables is a red flag. Tables stay tables only when exact values, feature matrices, or many discrete configuration dimensions are the point.
7. **Same RQ, same data → one float only.** Within a single RQ or experiment block, the same dataset must not appear as both a table and a figure. Pick the format that best serves the claim: a figure for trends, comparisons, and distributions; a table for exact values, feature matrices, or many discrete dimensions. If a figure needs exact numbers, annotate its bars/lines instead of adding a companion table. Duplicate presentation wastes page budget and forces the reader to cross-reference two floats for the same point.

Figure content and figure placement fail independently — check both. For two-column papers:

- **Wide figures span both columns**: use `figure*` (and `table*`); a wide figure squeezed into one column is unreadable. `figure*` cannot use `[h]`; it floats to the top of a page.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate RQ1 and RQ3 figures for the AgentPProf paper."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 10,
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'figure.figsize': (3.5, 2.5),
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.alpha': 0.3,
})

BLUE = '#2196F3'
RED = '#E57373'
GRAY = '#9E9E9E'


def make_rq1_separation():
    labels = ['No semantic\ntags', 'Session\ntag only', 'Prompt\ntag only', 'Session\n+ Prompt']
    mixed = [90.4, 84.4, 36.7, 0.0]
    residual = [44.7, 33.4, 7.5, 0.0]
    stacks = [11967, 15027, 24703, 26829]

    x = np.arange(len(labels))
    width = 0.28

    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.5))

    b1 = ax1.bar(x - width/2, mixed, width, label='Mixed weight %',
                 color=RED, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')
    b2 = ax1.bar(x + width/2, residual, width, label='Residual %',
                 color='#FFAB91', alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax1.set_ylabel('Percentage (%)', fontsize=8)
    ax1.set_xticks(x)
    ax1.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=7)
    ax1.set_ylim(0, 115)
    ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

    for i, m in enumerate(mixed):
        if m > 5:
            ax1.text(i - width/2, m + 1.5, f'{m:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                     fontsize=6, color=RED, fontweight='bold')
    for i, r in enumerate(residual):
        if r > 5:
            ax1.text(i + width/2, r + 1.5, f'{r:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                     fontsize=6, color='#E64A19', fontweight='bold')

    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    ax2.plot(x, [s/1000 for s in stacks], 's-', color=BLUE, linewidth=1.5,
             markersize=4, label='Unique stacks (k)', zorder=5)
    ax2.set_ylabel('Unique stacks (k)', fontsize=8)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 35)
    ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

    for i, s in enumerate(stacks):
        ax2.text(i, s/1000 + 1.0, f'{s/1000:.1f}k', ha='center', va='bottom',
                 fontsize=6, color=BLUE, fontweight='bold')

    h1, l1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
    h2, l2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(h1 + h2, l1 + l2, fontsize=6.5,
               loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.02),
               ncol=3, framealpha=0.9, columnspacing=0.8)

    plt.tight_layout()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate RQ1 and RQ3 figures for the AgentPProf paper."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 10,
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'figure.figsize': (3.5, 2.5),
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.alpha': 0.3,
})

BLUE = '#2196F3'
RED = '#E57373'
GRAY = '#9E9E9E'


def make_rq1_separation():
    labels = ['No semantic\ntags', 'Session\ntag only', 'Prompt\ntag only', 'Session\n+ Prompt']
    mixed = [90.4, 84.4, 36.7, 0.0]
    residual = [44.7, 33.4, 7.5, 0.0]
    stacks = [11967, 15027, 24703, 26829]

    x = np.arange(len(labels))
    width = 0.28

    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.5))

    b1 = ax1.bar(x - width/2, mixed, width, label='Mixed weight %',
                 color=RED, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')
    b2 = ax1.bar(x + width/2, residual, width, label='Residual %',
                 color='#FFAB91', alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax1.set_ylabel('Percentage (%)', fontsize=8)
    ax1.set_xticks(x)
    ax1.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=7)
    ax1.set_ylim(0, 115)
    ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

    for i, m in enumerate(mixed):
        if m > 5:
            ax1.text(i - width/2, m + 1.5, f'{m:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                     fontsize=6, color=RED, fontweight='bold')
    for i, r in enumerate(residual):
        if r > 5:
            ax1.text(i + width/2, r + 1.5, f'{r:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                     fontsize=6, color='#E64A19', fontweight='bold')

    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    ax2.plot(x, [s/1000 for s in stacks], 's-', color=BLUE, linewidth=1.5,
             markersize=4, label='Unique stacks (k)', zorder=5)
    ax2.set_ylabel('Unique stacks (k)', fontsize=8)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 35)
    ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

    for i, s in enumerate(stacks):
        ax2.text(i, s/1000 + 1.0, f'{s/1000:.1f}k', ha='center', va='bottom',
                 fontsize=6, color=BLUE, fontweight='bold')

    h1, l1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
    h2, l2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(h1 + h2, l1 + l2, fontsize=6.5,
               loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.02),
               ncol=3, framealpha=0.9, columnspacing=0.8)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq1-separation.pdf/png')


def make_rq3_vmeasure():
    datasets = ['mind2web', 'webshop', 'swe-agent', 'weblinx',
                'agenttrek', 'gui-odyssey', 'android', 'toolbench', 'api-bank']
    vmeasure =    [1.000, 1.000, 0.926, 0.872, 0.862, 0.811, 0.716, 0.134, 0.000]
    boundary_f1 = [1.000, 1.000, 0.962, 0.860, None,  0.842, 0.727, 0.353, None]
    ops =         [774,   2504,  496,   500,   200,   7868,  9,     866,   48]

    x = np.arange(len(datasets))
    width = 0.35

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.8))

    vm_colors = [BLUE if v >= 0.7 else GRAY for v in vmeasure]
    bf_colors = ['#81D4FA' if (b is not None and b >= 0.7) else '#BDBDBD'
                 for b in boundary_f1]

    ax.bar(x - width/2, vmeasure, width, color=vm_colors, alpha=0.85,
           edgecolor='white', label='V-measure')

    bf_vals = [b if b is not None else 0 for b in boundary_f1]
    ax.bar(x + width/2, bf_vals, width, color=bf_colors, alpha=0.85,
           edgecolor='white', label='Boundary F1')
    for i, b in enumerate(boundary_f1):
        if b is None:
            ax.text(i + width/2, 0.02, '---', ha='center', va='bottom',
                    fontsize=5, color=GRAY)

    ax.axhline(y=0.7, color=RED, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.0, label='Threshold (0.7)')
    ax.set_ylabel('Score')
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(datasets, fontsize=6, rotation=40, ha='right')
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.18)
    ax.legend(fontsize=6, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9, ncol=1)

    for i, (v, o) in enumerate(zip(vmeasure, ops)):
        if v > 0.05:
            ax.text(i - width/2, v + 0.02, f'{v:.2f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                    fontsize=5, color='#1565C0')
        label = f'{o/1000:.1f}k' if o >= 1000 else str(o)
        ax.text(i, -0.08, label, ha='center', va='top', fontsize=4.5, color=GRAY)
    ax.text(-0.8, -0.08, 'ops:', ha='right', va='top', fontsize=4.5, color=GRAY)

    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.subplots_adjust(bottom=0.25)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq3-vmeasure.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq3-vmeasure.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq3-vmeasure.pdf/png')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    make_rq1_separation()
    make_rq3_vmeasure()

# Result Plots for Systems Papers

Bar charts, line plots, CDFs, heatmaps, and table-as-figure for evaluation sections.

## Purpose

A result plot answers: **"Does the system achieve claim X?"** Every plot must support a specific claim. If you can't name the claim, the plot may be unnecessary.

## One plot, one question

Each figure should answer ONE research question:
- "How does startup latency compare to baselines?" → bar chart
- "How does throughput scale with load?" → line plot
- "What is the tail latency distribution?" → CDF
- "Where does time go?" → stacked bar or breakdown

Do NOT pack multiple unrelated comparisons into one figure unless they share axes and the comparison is the point.

## Plot types and when to use them

| Question | Plot type | Example |
|----------|----------|---------|
| Compare discrete values | Bar chart | Startup: Sandlock vs Docker vs bare metal |
| Show trend over continuous variable | Line plot | Throughput vs number of concurrent tools |
| Show distribution | CDF or histogram | Latency distribution across runs |
| Show breakdown | Stacked bar | Time breakdown: confinement vs execution |
| Compare many systems × many metrics | Table | Feature comparison (Table 1 style) |
| Show 2D relationship | Heatmap or scatter | Memory vs CPU across workloads |

## Design principles

### Baselines
- Always include a meaningful baseline (bare metal, no confinement, existing system)
- Label baselines clearly — "Bare metal" not "Baseline 1"
- If comparing against Docker, state the configuration (bridge vs host networking, rootful vs rootless)

### Axes
- Label both axes with units: "Latency (ms)", "Throughput (krps)", "Memory (MB)"
- Start y-axis at 0 unless there's a strong reason not to (and state why)
- Use consistent scales across sub-figures if comparing

### Error bars and statistics
- Always show variance: error bars (std dev or CI), or report median + percentiles
- State the number of runs: "median of 20 runs after warm-up"
- If differences are small, state whether they are within run-to-run variance

### Labels and legends
- Use descriptive names: "Sandlock" not "System A"
- Keep legends inside the plot area if space permits
- Order legend entries to match visual order (top-to-bottom or left-to-right)

### Colors
- Use colorblind-safe palette (avoid red-green only distinction)
- Use consistent colors across all figures (Sandlock = same color everywhere)
- Black/white should be distinguishable (patterns or markers for grayscale printing)

### Multi-panel figures
- Use (a), (b), (c) labels
- Share axes where meaningful
- Reference sub-figures explicitly: "Figure 2(a)" not just "Figure 2"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate RQ1 and RQ3 figures for the AgentPProf paper."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 10,
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'figure.figsize': (3.5, 2.5),
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.alpha': 0.3,
})

BLUE = '#2196F3'
RED = '#E57373'
GRAY = '#9E9E9E'


def make_rq1_separation():
    labels = ['No semantic\ntags', 'Session\ntag only', 'Prompt\ntag only', 'Session\n+ Prompt']
    mixed = [90.4, 84.4, 36.7, 0.0]
    residual = [44.7, 33.4, 7.5, 0.0]
    stacks = [11967, 15027, 24703, 26829]

    x = np.arange(len(labels))
    width = 0.28

    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.5))

    b1 = ax1.bar(x - width/2, mixed, width, label='Mixed weight %',
                 color=RED, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')
    b2 = ax1.bar(x + width/2, residual, width, label='Residual %',
                 color='#FFAB91', alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white')

    ax1.set_ylabel('Percentage (%)', fontsize=8)
    ax1.set_xticks(x)
    ax1.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=7)
    ax1.set_ylim(0, 115)
    ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

    for i, m in enumerate(mixed):
        if m > 5:
            ax1.text(i - width/2, m + 1.5, f'{m:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                     fontsize=6, color=RED, fontweight='bold')
    for i, r in enumerate(residual):
        if r > 5:
            ax1.text(i + width/2, r + 1.5, f'{r:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                     fontsize=6, color='#E64A19', fontweight='bold')

    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    ax2.plot(x, [s/1000 for s in stacks], 's-', color=BLUE, linewidth=1.5,
             markersize=4, label='Unique stacks (k)', zorder=5)
    ax2.set_ylabel('Unique stacks (k)', fontsize=8)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 35)
    ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

    for i, s in enumerate(stacks):
        ax2.text(i, s/1000 + 1.0, f'{s/1000:.1f}k', ha='center', va='bottom',
                 fontsize=6, color=BLUE, fontweight='bold')

    h1, l1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
    h2, l2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(h1 + h2, l1 + l2, fontsize=6.5,
               loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.02),
               ncol=3, framealpha=0.9, columnspacing=0.8)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq1-separation.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq1-separation.pdf/png')


def make_rq3_vmeasure():
    datasets = ['mind2web', 'webshop', 'swe-agent', 'weblinx',
                'agenttrek', 'gui-odyssey', 'android', 'toolbench', 'api-bank']
    vmeasure =    [1.000, 1.000, 0.926, 0.872, 0.862, 0.811, 0.716, 0.134, 0.000]
    boundary_f1 = [1.000, 1.000, 0.962, 0.860, None,  0.842, 0.727, 0.353, None]
    ops =         [774,   2504,  496,   500,   200,   7868,  9,     866,   48]

    x = np.arange(len(datasets))
    width = 0.35

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.8))

    vm_colors = [BLUE if v >= 0.7 else GRAY for v in vmeasure]
    bf_colors = ['#81D4FA' if (b is not None and b >= 0.7) else '#BDBDBD'
                 for b in boundary_f1]

    ax.bar(x - width/2, vmeasure, width, color=vm_colors, alpha=0.85,
           edgecolor='white', label='V-measure')

    bf_vals = [b if b is not None else 0 for b in boundary_f1]
    ax.bar(x + width/2, bf_vals, width, color=bf_colors, alpha=0.85,
           edgecolor='white', label='Boundary F1')
    for i, b in enumerate(boundary_f1):
        if b is None:
            ax.text(i + width/2, 0.02, '---', ha='center', va='bottom',
                    fontsize=5, color=GRAY)

    ax.axhline(y=0.7, color=RED, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.0, label='Threshold (0.7)')
    ax.set_ylabel('Score')
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(datasets, fontsize=6, rotation=40, ha='right')
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.18)
    ax.legend(fontsize=6, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9, ncol=1)

    for i, v in enumerate(vmeasure):
        if v > 0.05:
            ax.text(i - width/2, v + 0.02, f'{v:.2f}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                    fontsize=5, color='#1565C0')

    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('fig-rq3-vmeasure.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    plt.savefig('fig-rq3-vmeasure.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
    print('Wrote fig-rq3-vmeasure.pdf/png')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    make_rq1_separation()
    make_rq3_vmeasure()

**RQ2 的表和图不是同一数据的重复**——这是合理的：

- **表** (`tab:localization`): 7 个 policy × 8 个指标 = 56 个精确数值，这正是"feature matrix"的用法，适合表格
- **图** (`fig:rq2-tradeoff`): scatter plot 展示 Work@5 vs R@30% 的 tradeoff 关系，这是表里读不出的视觉洞察

它们互补而非重复。表提供完整精确值，图突出 tradeoff 趋势。按 skill 的规则，"many discrete dimensions"应该用表，tradeoff scatter 应该用图——各司其职。

其他地方：`tab:views` 和 `fig:architecture` 分别是不同内容（视图定义 vs 系统架构图），不重复。`fig:flamegraph` 是独立的。

现在检查 RQ1 正文的结论部分——你说还没讲清楚 eval 能得出什么结论。

560	\subsection{RQ1: Does Semantic Profiling Improve Resource Attribution?}
561	% RQ1：语义分析能否改善资源归因？
562	
563	The strongest argument against semantic profiling is that traditional tools ``can already see the same information.''
564	% 反对语义分析的最强论点是传统工具"已经能看到相同信息"。
565	To test this, we run a semantic-axis ablation on 325 real Codex/Claude trajectories (183{,}714 system observations).
566	% 为了检验这一点，我们在 325 个真实 Codex/Claude 会话（183,714 个系统观测）上进行语义轴消融。
567	We progressively add tag axes (no tags, session only, prompt only, both) and measure the mixed-weight percentage, the fraction of system-effect cost in groups that mix observations from multiple task categories.
568	% 我们逐步添加标签轴（无标签、仅会话、仅提示词、两者兼有），测量混合权重百分比——混合了多个任务类别观测的桶中的系统副作用权重比例。
569	A lower mixed-weight percentage means the profiler correctly separates effects by task category.
570	% 更低的混合权重百分比意味着分析器正确地按任务类别分离了效果。
571	The residual percentage measures weight in groups where the majority category accounts for less than 90\% of the group, capturing partial mixing.
572	% 残余百分比测量多数类别占桶内不到 90\% 的权重，捕获部分混合。
573	
574	Figure~\ref{fig:rq1-separation} shows the result.
575	% Figure~\ref{fig:rq1-separation} 展示了结果。
576	Without semantic tags, nearly all system-effect cost falls into mixed groups: a flat \texttt{cargo~test} counter shows 2{,}903 executions but cannot distinguish whether they came from \texttt{review}, \texttt{debug}, \texttt{refactor}, or \texttt{test} prompts.
577	% 没有语义标签时，几乎所有系统副作用权重落入混合桶：扁平的 \texttt{cargo test} 计数器显示 2,903 次执行，但无法区分来源。
578	The prompt tag is the decisive axis: it drops both mixed weight and residual by more than half and nearly doubles the number of unique stacks, because it separates observations that share the same system call but originate from different task intents.
579	% 提示词标签是决定性轴：它将混合权重和残余都降低一半以上，唯一栈数量几乎翻倍，因为它分离了共享相同系统调用但来自不同任务意图的观测。
580	The session tag alone barely helps because trajectories typically contain multiple intent phases.
581	% 仅会话标签几乎没有帮助，因为会话通常包含多个意图阶段。
582	
583	A tag-permutation test (1{,}000 shuffles, $p = 0.001$) confirms the separation is not random.
584	% 标签置换测试（1,000 次洗牌，$p = 0.001$）确认分离不是随机的。
585	Semantic-tag quality is validated in RQ3.
586	% 语义标签质量在 RQ3 中验证。
587	
588	Beyond tag separation, we test whether choosing different field selections for the operation stack produces views that flat grouping cannot.
589	% 除标签分离外，我们还测试为 operation stack 选择不同字段是否产生扁平分组无法产生的视图。
590	We take the same 13{,}265 operations from the four families with ground-truth annotations and fold them with five different field selections, counting how many distinct groups each produces.
591	% 我们取四个有真实标注的家族的同样 13,265 个 operation，用五种不同字段选择折叠，计算每种产生多少不同分组。
592	The same operations fold into 9~dataset groups, 57~phase groups, 226~semantic groups, 455~action groups, or 3{,}757~per-session groups by changing only the stack fields.
593	% 同样的 operation 仅通过改变栈字段即可折叠为 9 个数据集分组、57 个阶段分组、226 个语义分组、455 个操作分组或 3,757 个固定会话分组。
594	A flat GROUP BY on a single tag cannot produce these views because different stack depths answer different questions (budget by task vs.\ duplication by action vs.\ per-session detail).
595	% 单标签的扁平 GROUP BY 无法产生这些视图，因为不同栈深度回答不同问题（任务级预算 vs. 操作级重复 vs. 会话级下钻）。
596	The same model also covers all 15 public trajectory families without type-specific objects.
597	% 同一模型也覆盖了所有 15 个公开 trace 家族，无需特定类型对象。
598	
599	Different views also produce different rankings.
600	% 不同视图也产生不同排名。
601	The \texttt{time} and \texttt{tokens} views of the same 325 trajectories share only 7/10 top prompt categories (Spearman $\rho = 0.623$).
602	% 同一 325 个会话的 \texttt{time} 和 \texttt{tokens} 视图仅共享 7/10 的顶级提示词类别（Spearman $\rho = 0.623$）。
603	\texttt{network}-tagged prompts rank 8th by time (I/O wait) but 93rd by tokens, showing that the choice of weight function changes the analysis conclusions.
604	% \texttt{network} 标记的提示词按时间排第 8（I/O 等待）但按 token 排第 93，表明权重函数的选择改变了分析结论。
605	
606	Finally, we test whether the profiler can produce useful groups without any user-specified fields.
607	% 最后，我们测试分析器能否在不需要任何用户指定字段的情况下产生有用的分组。
608	We run the automatic stack-induction mode (\S\ref{sec:stacks}) on the same six tasks used in RQ2 and compare the resulting group count and localization quality against flat summaries and per-session grouping.
609	% 我们在 RQ2 使用的同样六个任务上运行自动栈诱导模式（\S\ref{sec:stacks}），将结果的分组数和定位质量与扁平摘要和固定会话下钻进行比较。
610	Induced stacks produce a median of 12 groups (versus 285 for per-session and 1 for flat), with 4/6 tasks generating variable-depth stacks.
611	% 诱导栈产生中位 12 个分组（固定会话 285 个，扁平 1 个），4/6 任务生成可变深度栈。
612	The induced stacks achieve lower AP than hand-configured stacks (median 0.276 vs 0.312) because they use only visible fields, but they reduce inspection work to 65.3\% versus flat summaries without requiring any user configuration.
613	% 诱导栈的 AP 低于手动配置栈（中位 0.276 vs 0.312），因为它们仅使用可见字段，但将检查工作量降至扁平摘要的 65.3\%，无需任何用户配置。
614	
615	Figure~\ref{fig:flamegraph} shows the resulting flame graphs for the \texttt{tokens} and \texttt{files} views, illustrating that changing only the stack fields and weight function produces different aggregates from the same operations.
616	% Figure~\ref{fig:flamegraph} 展示了 \texttt{tokens} 和 \texttt{files} 视图的火焰图，说明仅改变栈字段和权重函数即可从同一组 operation 产生不同聚合。
617

\subsection{RQ1: Does Semantic Profiling Improve Resource Attribution?}
% RQ1：语义分析能否改善资源归因？

The strongest argument against semantic profiling is that traditional tools ``can already see the same information.''
% 反对语义分析的最强论点是传统工具"已经能看到相同信息"。
To test this, we run a semantic-axis ablation on 325 real Codex/Claude trajectories (183{,}714 system observations).
% 为了检验这一点，我们在 325 个真实 Codex/Claude 会话（183,714 个系统观测）上进行语义轴消融。
We progressively add tag axes (no tags, session only, prompt only, both) and measure the mixed-weight percentage, the fraction of system-effect cost in groups that mix observations from multiple task categories.
% 我们逐步添加标签轴（无标签、仅会话、仅提示词、两者兼有），测量混合权重百分比——混合了多个任务类别观测的桶中的系统副作用权重比例。
A lower mixed-weight percentage means the profiler correctly separates effects by task category.
% 更低的混合权重百分比意味着分析器正确地按任务类别分离了效果。
The residual percentage measures weight in groups where the majority category accounts for less than 90\% of the group, capturing partial mixing.
% 残余百分比测量多数类别占桶内不到 90\% 的权重，捕获部分混合。

Figure~\ref{fig:rq1-separation} shows the result.
% Figure~\ref{fig:rq1-separation} 展示了结果。
Without semantic tags, nearly all system-effect cost falls into mixed groups: a flat \texttt{cargo~test} counter shows 2{,}903 executions but cannot distinguish whether they came from \texttt{review}, \texttt{debug}, \texttt{refactor}, or \texttt{test} prompts.
% 没有语义标签时，几乎所有系统副作用权重落入混合桶：扁平的 \texttt{cargo test} 计数器显示 2,903 次执行，但无法区分来源。
The prompt tag is the decisive axis: it drops both mixed weight and residual by more than half and nearly doubles the number of unique stacks, because it separates observations that share the same system call but originate from different task intents.
% 提示词标签是决定性轴：它将混合权重和残余都降低一半以上，唯一栈数量几乎翻倍，因为它分离了共享相同系统调用但来自不同任务意图的观测。
The session tag alone barely helps because trajectories typically contain multiple intent phases.
% 仅会话标签几乎没有帮助，因为会话通常包含多个意图阶段。

A tag-permutation test (1{,}000 shuffles, $p = 0.001$) confirms the separation is not random.
% 标签置换测试（1,000 次洗牌，$p = 0.001$）确认分离不是随机的。
Semantic-tag quality is validated in RQ3.
% 语义标签质量在 RQ3 中验证。

Beyond tag separation, we test whether choosing different field selections for the operation stack produces views that flat grouping cannot.
% 除标签分离外，我们还测试为 operation stack 选择不同字段是否产生扁平分组无法产生的视图。
We take the same 13{,}265 operations from the four families with ground-truth annotations and fold them with five different field selections, counting how many distinct groups each produces.
% 我们取四个有真实标注的家族的同样 13,265 个 operation，用五种不同字段选择折叠，计算每种产生多少不同分组。
The same operations fold into 9~dataset groups, 57~phase groups, 226~semantic groups, 455~action groups, or 3{,}757~per-session groups by changing only the stack fields.
% 同样的 operation 仅通过改变栈字段即可折叠为 9 个数据集分组、57 个阶段分组、226 个语义分组、455 个操作分组或 3,757 个固定会话分组。
A flat GROUP BY on a single tag cannot produce these views because different stack depths answer different questions (budget by task vs.\ duplication by action vs.\ per-session detail).
% 单标签的扁平 GROUP BY 无法产生这些视图，因为不同栈深度回答不同问题（任务级预算 vs. 操作级重复 vs. 会话级下钻）。
The same model also covers all 15 public trajectory families without type-specific objects.
% 同一模型也覆盖了所有 15 个公开 trace 家族，无需特定类型对象。

Different views also produce different rankings.
% 不同视图也产生不同排名。
The \texttt{time} and \texttt{tokens} views of the same 325 trajectories share only 7/10 top prompt categories (Spearman $\rho = 0.623$).
% 同一 325 个会话的 \texttt{time} 和 \texttt{tokens} 视图仅共享 7/10 的顶级提示词类别（Spearman $\rho = 0.623$）。
\texttt{network}-tagged prompts rank 8th by time (I/O wait) but 93rd by tokens, showing that the choice of weight function changes the analysis conclusions.
% \texttt{network} 标记的提示词按时间排第 8（I/O 等待）但按 token 排第 93，表明权重函数的选择改变了分析结论。

Finally, we test whether the profiler can produce useful groups without any user-specified fields.
% 最后，我们测试分析器能否在不需要任何用户指定字段的情况下产生有用的分组。
We run the automatic stack-induction mode (\S\ref{sec:stacks}) on the same six tasks used in RQ2 and compare the resulting group count and localization quality against flat summaries and per-session grouping.
% 我们在 RQ2 使用的同样六个任务上运行自动栈诱导模式（\S\ref{sec:stacks}），将结果的分组数和定位质量与扁平摘要和固定会话下钻进行比较。
Induced stacks produce a median of 12 groups (versus 285 for per-session and 1 for flat), with 4/6 tasks generating variable-depth stacks.
% 诱导栈产生中位 12 个分组（固定会话 285 个，扁平 1 个），4/6 任务生成可变深度栈。

27	%% S1: Context (→¶1)
28	AI agents increasingly orchestrate long-running, multi-step
29	activities involving thousands to millions of interactions with

31	% AI 智能体编排长时间运行的多步骤活动，涉及与用户、工具和系统资源的数千到数百万次交互。

37	%% S3: Traditional profiling (→¶2+¶4)
38	To answer similar questions in traditional systems software, profiling
39	attributes resource consumption to responsible entities, such as code
40	paths, by aggregation, rather than single-execution debugging or
41	tracing.
42	% 在传统系统软件中，profiling 通过聚合将资源消耗归因到负责实体（如代码路径），而非单次执行调试或 tracing。
43	%% S4: Gap (→¶2+¶3)
44	Yet existing agent observability tools are mainly for debugging and
45	tracing instead of profiling.
46	% 然而现有智能体可观测性工具主要用于调试和 tracing，而非 profiling。
47	%% S5: Agent challenge (→¶4)
48	Agent behavior differs fundamentally from code execution.
49	The responsible entities are semantic categories such as task intent
50	and workflow phase, not code paths, and agent trajectories lack the
51	stable identifiers and structural hierarchies that make
52	aggregation possible.
53	% 智能体行为与代码执行有根本不同。负责实体是语义类别（如任务意图和工作流阶段），而非代码路径，且智能体轨迹缺乏使聚合成为可能的稳定标识符和结构层次。
54	%% S6: Model (→¶5)
55	We propose a \emph{semantic operation stack model} that
56	adapts profiling to agent trajectories.
57	Uniform \emph{operations} represent all agent activities, and
58	\emph{operation stacks} replace the runtime call stack with
59	query-time field projections that fold identical frame sequences.
60	% 我们提出首个将 profiling 适配到智能体轨迹的语义 operation stack 模型。统一的 operation 表示所有智能体活动，operation stack 用查询时字段投影替代运行时调用栈，折叠相同帧序列。
61	%% S7: System (→¶6)

63	for \emph{intent attribution} and \emph{stack construction},
64	compiling local agent trajectories into pprof-compatible profiles.

66	%% S8: Results (→¶6)
67	On real trajectories and public datasets, our evaluation shows that
68	semantic profiling effectively attributes cost and locates problems
69	across agent trajectories.
70	% 在真实轨迹和公开数据集上，我们的评估表明语义 profiling 能有效地跨智能体轨迹归因开销和定位问题。
71	\end{abstract}

76	\section{Introduction}
77	\label{sec:intro}
78	
79	%% ¶1: Background + context
80	AI agents~\cite{sweagent,claudecode,osworld} orchestrate multi-step activities that span two layers, high-level intent (prompts, LLM calls, tool invocations) and low-level system effects (process spawns, file and network I/O).
81	% AI 智能体~\cite{sweagent,claudecode,osworld}编排跨越两层的多步骤活动：高层意图（提示词、LLM 调用、工具调用）和低层系统副作用（进程创建、文件和网络 I/O）。
82	As agents evolve from short, scripted workflows into complex systems that run for hours and days, with a large number of interactions each, production teams accumulate many such trajectories over weeks or months.
83	% 随着智能体从短小的脚本化工作流进化为每次运行数小时、包含数千次交互的复杂系统，生产团队在数周或数月内积累大量此类轨迹。
84	
85	%% ¶2: Problem
86	To improve agent quality, safety, and cost efficiency, developers
87	need to analyze operational behavior across trajectories and
88	interactions.
89	Which categories of tasks consume the most token budget? Where do
90	failures concentrate across workflows? Which behavioral patterns
91	trigger unsafe system effects?
92	% 为了提高智能体质量、安全性和成本效率，开发者需要跨轨迹和交互分析运维行为。哪类任务消耗最多 token 预算？故障跨工作流集中在哪里？哪些行为模式触发不安全系统副作用？
93	Answering these questions requires analysis and evaluation across many
94	trajectories~\cite{agentatlas,agentrewardbench}, a task becoming costly for manual inspection or
95	per-trajectory LLM evaluation~\cite{llm-as-judge} at scale.
96	% 回答这些问题需要跨许多轨迹的分析和评估，在规模化时人工检查或逐轨迹 LLM 评估的成本越来越高。
97	In traditional systems software, profiling answers these questions by
98	attributing resource consumption to responsible entities by
99	aggregation, as distinct from single-execution debugging and tracing.
100	% 在传统系统软件中，profiling 通过聚合将资源消耗归因到负责实体来回答这些问题，区别于单次执行调试和 tracing。
101	
102	%% ¶3: Existing solutions
103	Yet existing agent tools support debugging and tracing but not
104	profiling (\S\ref{sec:background}).
105	% 然而现有智能体工具支持调试和 tracing，但不支持 profiling（\S\ref{sec:background}）。
106	Some~\cite{langsmith,langfuse,phoenix,otel} organize events into
107	per-execution span trees, effective for diagnosing a single run but
108	unable to aggregate by semantic category.
109	% 一些工具~\cite{langsmith,langfuse,phoenix,otel}将事件组织为按执行划分的 span 树，有效诊断单次运行但无法按语义类别聚合。
110	Others~\cite{datadog-llmobs,laminar-signals} cluster inputs or
111	extract structured signals, but characterize \emph{input
112	distributions} (``30\% of users ask code questions'') rather than
113	\emph{resource attribution} (``review tasks consume 40\% of the
114	token budget''), because tags at the request level do not propagate
115	to downstream tool calls and system effects.
116	% 另一些~\cite{datadog-llmobs,laminar-signals}聚类输入或提取结构化信号，但刻画的是输入分布（"30\% 的用户提问代码问题"）而非资源归因（"review 任务消耗了 40\% 的 token 预算"），因为请求级的标签不会传播到下游工具调用和系统副作用。
117	
118	%% ¶4: Challenge — why traditional profiling doesn't transfer directly
119	Adapting profiling to agent trajectories is challenging
120	(\S\ref{sec:background}).
121	% 将 profiling 适配到智能体轨迹具有挑战性（\S\ref{sec:background}）。
122	In traditional software, the responsible entities are code paths.
123	Profiling is straightforward because function names are

139	tool calls, and system effects are not nested by execution the way

这张图的含义：

- **X 轴 (Median top-5 inspected work)**：检查前 5 个分组需要看多少工作量占总量的比例。越小越好——意味着只看少量数据就能覆盖重要分组。
- **Y 轴 (Median budget-30 recall)**：在只检查 30% 工作量的预算下，能召回多少真实问题（故障/安全违规/冗余步骤）。越高越好。
- **每个点**是一种分组策略（Flat、Fixed-session、Op-stack query 等）

理想位置是**左上角**（少量检查工作、高召回）。图上可以看到：
- **Flat**（灰色，右下）：必须检查全部内容，召回为 0（因为只有 1 个分组，无法区分）
- **Op-stack query**（绿色）：在左侧中间，检查约 9% 就能召回约 39% 的问题
- **Oracle**（深绿/黄色，左上）：上界

这张图和表不重复——表给了 7 个 policy 的 8 个精确指标值，图只选了其中两个维度（Work@5 vs R@30%）画 tradeoff 关系，让读者一眼看到各策略在"效率 vs 召回"空间里的位置。表里的 AP、F1@5、WTFP、Groups 等指标图上看不到。

\caption{RQ2: Inspection work vs.\ recall at 30\% inspection budget.

fragments into 285 groups. Oracle policies (large dots) are upper bounds.}
\Description{Scatter plot showing inspection work versus budget recall

The profiler's configuration is also actionable.

Modifying stack fields, mapping rules, or ranking criteria and re-running on the same operations improves AP on 5/6 tasks (median AP improvement 0.038), confirming that the profiler exposes useful tuning knobs rather than requiring a fixed configuration.

\subsection{RQ3: How Accurate Are the Tags?}

% 分析开销是会话结束后花费的时间和资源。

We re-execute 76 tracked profiling configurations twice (152 invocations) to measure cost and verify determinism.
% 我们重新执行 76 个跟踪的 profiling configuration 两次（152 次调用）来测量开销并验证确定性。
All 76 configurations produce byte-identical output across both runs.
% 全部 76 个配置在两次运行中产生字节相同的输出。
Median profiling time is 1.6\,s per configuration (p95 2.8\,s, max 4.3\,s), and median output size is 37.5\,KB.
% 中位分析时间为每配置 1.6 秒（p95 2.8 秒，最大 4.3 秒），中位输出大小为 37.5 KB。
The slowest configurations process views with over 600 unique stacks, while the 60 robustness configurations all complete within 1.6\,s.
% 最慢的配置处理超过 600 个唯一栈的视图，而 60 个稳健性配置全部在 1.6 秒内完成。
The full configuration space (operation files, query predicates, ranking criteria, and stack depth) stays deterministic across all 12 tested variants.
% 完整的配置空间（operation 文件、查询谓词、排名标准和栈深度）在所有 12 个测试变体中保持确定性。

Intent attribution adds a one-time cost for new prompts.
% 意图归因对新提示词增加一次性开销。
Of 118{,}021 tag requests on 325 real trajectories, 70\% are cache hits (zero cost), and the remaining 35{,}136 new calls complete at p95 latency of 31\,ms per tag using a local 3B-parameter model.
% 在 325 个真实会话的 118,021 个标注请求中，70\% 为缓存命中（零开销），其余 35,136 个新调用使用本地 3B 参数模型以 p95 延迟 31 毫秒/标签完成。
Grammar-constrained decoding ensures 100\% syntax validity (2{,}700/2{,}700 test tags).
% 语法约束解码确保 100\% 语法有效性（2,700/2,700 测试标签）。
Because tags are cached, re-profiling the same trajectories with different stack fields or predicates incurs no additional LLM calls.
% 因为标签被缓存，用不同栈字段或谓词重新分析相同会话不产生额外 LLM 调用。
